transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 11:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Diego (Redwood) — Priya, Tom, Asha (Solstice)

Summary / quick notes (auto): Maya opened, Diego walked throughput telemetry, Priya asked about cache durability and data residency, Tom wants concrete replay steps. Agreed actions and due dates at end.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick check-in, we have about 40 minutes. how's last week's batch experiment look for you priya?

[00:18] Priya Nair: hey maya, yeah thanks. we ran the 128->256 batch increase on the staging traffic slice. learned a few things, latency p50 moved up from 86ms to 130ms and p95 jumped a bit, but tokens/sec improved by roughly 1.9x. cost per token down but user-facing latency is edging up.

[00:36] Diego Ruiz: ok that matches our charts. so on our side we see the same improvements in throughput. the thing to watch is tail latency, especially when requests have long generations; batching helps average cost but can amplify p95.

[00:51] Tom Briggs: yeah we saw some jitter during peak windows, the app-level timeout currently 400ms so a higher p95 risks user errors. can we push smarter routing or timeout fallback?

[01:06] Diego Ruiz: absolutely. two levers: adaptive batching (smaller max batch at low queue delay) and fast-fail fallback to a smaller model or lower temperature variant. we can do canary routing so critical endpoints use lower-batch, lower-latency path.

[01:22] Asha Patel: quick question — caching: when you say prefix or KV cache, are we talking about reuse across sessions or per-user cache? we would like to know privacy/retention implications.

[01:36] Maya Chen: good callout. KV/prefix cache is typically per model instance and can be configured to not persist beyond the inference lifecycle. for Solstice's use case, short-lived prefix cache (per session) gives most benefit; you can also encrypt things in transit and tie to key scope. we'll send the security doc link.

[01:52] Priya Nair: perfect. we ran an experiment enabling naive prefix caching for repeated product-descriptions and saw 22% token reduction and latency improved by 12% on average. caveat: our dataset had high repetition. results vary by prompt entropy.

[02:08] Diego Ruiz: yes repetition helps a lot. in our benchmarks we typically see 15-35% token savings for prompts with heavy prefix reuse. important to measure the hit rate; lower hit rate and cache overhead can negate wins.

[02:24] Tom Briggs: on cost math, we're trying to reconcile tokens/sec per dollar numbers in the spreadsheet. priya mentioned a 1.9x improvement — can you walk the group through the math diego?

[02:38] Diego Ruiz: sure. baseline small model at batch 128: we were at 8.2k tokens/sec per GPU and effective cost $0.45 per 1k tokens (hosted assumptions). bumping to batch 256 increased effective tokens/sec to 15.4k so cost per 1k tokens dropped to ~0.24 — roughly half. but remember that per-request latency increased so per-user SLA cost may go up. also, model variant quantization changes cost; a 4-bit quantized variant reduces kernel compute by ~20-30% on our runtime.

[03:05] Priya Nair: that 4-bit number — is that across all sequence lengths? because some of our calls hit 2k tokens.

[03:13] Diego Ruiz: good question. the quantization savings are more pronounced at medium seq lengths, and for long sequences KV cache amortization matters. we can produce model-specific profiles for your common seq length distribution — we'll include that in the spreadsheet.

[03:28] Maya Chen: also note the routing fallback — if we route long-run requests to dedicated nodes with different batch policies you can keep tail latency manageable while still getting batching economics for short requests.

[03:40] Asha Patel: operationally, how invasive is enabling KV cache in our microservice? tom?

[03:48] Tom Briggs: from the staging test it required a small code change to pass session-id and read/write TTLs. main effort was infra and observability to ensure we don't leak. we'll need guidance from diego on config knobs.

[04:02] Diego Ruiz: I'll draft a 1-pager and a sample config. short version: session id in header, TTL controls, cache size cap per pod, and metrics for cache hit/miss. no persistent store required unless you opt-in for cross-pod sharing.

[04:18] Priya Nair: another item — data retention: our security team asked how long KV cache logs are retained and whether audit logs can be disabled for PII. is that something you support?

[04:32] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood's private deployments and dedicated offerings let you configure audit retention. hosted defaults to 90 days but we can offer project-level retention settings for enterprise. for PII we recommend token redaction and KMS for encryption at rest. we'll share the SOC2/ISO snippets.

[04:50] Tom Briggs: good. ok, about the spreadsheet: our finance team is sensitive to steady-state monthly spend projections. can we get a run of two scenarios: conservative (prioritize latency) and aggressive (prioritize cost)?

[05:03] Diego Ruiz: yes, we'll produce both: one with smaller batch caps and higher on-call reserve, and one with larger batch sizes and more aggressive KV caching assumptions. we'll annotate which assumptions are most sensitive.

[05:16] Asha Patel: is there an easy way to simulate real traffic for 24h without hitting prod?

[05:22] Tom Briggs: we have a replay infra, but need to know recommended RPS and typical session patterns — diego, what should we replay?

[05:30] Diego Ruiz: replay your staging logs at 70% of observed production RPS for 24h with realistic inter-arrival times. include the longer generation traces. that'll surface queueing and p95. also enable our diagnostic headers to capture batch sizes and queue delay.

[05:46] Priya Nair: and if we find that p95 is too high, what's the short-term mitigation?

[05:52] Maya Chen: immediate options: drop batch cap to 128, route long sessions to smaller-batch path, or enable a fallback smaller model for long runs. medium-term: dedicated capacity or autoscale buffer.

[06:05] Tom Briggs: can you quantify the cost delta for those mitigations? say dropping batch to 128 from 256 — how much cost increase per month?

[06:12] Diego Ruiz: we'll calculate; roughly doubling batch improves tokens/sec ~1.8-2x, so halving it reverses that. I'll put a per-100k-token estimate and a monthly projection in the spreadsheet.

[06:25] Asha Patel: on model variants, we tried the quantized 4-bit and saw some small quality drift on edge cases. what guardrails can we apply to detect regressions automatically?

[06:38] Diego Ruiz: recommended: automated evals on a representative prompt set with thresholds for perplexity/classification accuracy depending on your use case, plus sampling of live responses and a shadow evaluation route. Redwood Optimize can run those checks and alert on regression.

[06:52] Priya Nair: perfect. can Redwood run one eval on our sample prompt set? we can share it via the doc link later.

[06:58] Maya Chen: yes, we'll run it as part of the next week's work. please upload to shared drive; we'll kick off a baseline vs quantized comparison.

[07:08] Tom Briggs: small ops question — will enabling KV cache affect memory on the GPU instances? we noticed occasional OOMs in small nodes last week.

[07:15] Diego Ruiz: cache uses GPU host memory to store keys and values; it's configurable. default safe caps avoid OOMs, but if you push large sequence lengths and large cache sizes, you'll need larger instance types or cap the cache. we'll note recommended caps per instance family.

[07:35] Priya Nair: ok, great. what's the expected timeline for the spreadsheet and docs?

[07:40] Maya Chen: we'll have draft cost model + config doc by EOD 2026-11-05. diego's how-to on cache by 2026-11-04.

[07:48] Asha Patel: last question — any blockers on running the replay this week?

[07:52] Tom Briggs: none from infra; we just need the exact header props and RPS target.

[07:57] Diego Ruiz: I'll paste the replay command and diag headers in the spreadsheet.

[08:02] Maya Chen: ok let's recap. action items — maya will send spreadsheet, diego will prepare cache how-to and replay headers, tom will run replay, priya will confirm eval prompts. next sync same time next week unless we need a deep-dive sooner.

[08:20] Priya Nair: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[08:25] Tom Briggs: thanks.

[08:28] Diego Ruiz: thanks, bye.

[08:31] Maya Chen: bye.

Notes: transcript auto-stamped every ~15-40s. Occasional filler and minor mis-transcriptions present. References: cost_model_v2.csv (link shared in chat), security_and_retention_notes.pdf (will be shared).
